def filter_api_calls(
    logp_with_result: np.ndarray,
    logp_call_only: np.ndarray,
    logp_no_call: np.ndarray,
    tau_filter: float,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return an ordered keep mask and one finite margin per proposed call."""
    # Validate inputs
    if isinstance(tau_filter, bool):
        raise ValueError("tau_filter must be a float, not bool")
    if not np.issubdtype(type(tau_filter), np.floating) and not isinstance(tau_filter, (int, float)):
        raise ValueError("tau_filter must be a finite nonnegative float")
    if not np.isfinite(tau_filter) or tau_filter < 0:
        raise ValueError("tau_filter must be finite and nonnegative")

    for arr, name in [(logp_with_result, 'logp_with_result'), (logp_call_only, 'logp_call_only'), (logp_no_call, 'logp_no_call')]:
        if not isinstance(arr, np.ndarray) or arr.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a 2D NumPy array")
        if arr.size == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must not be empty")
        if np.any(np.isnan(arr)) or np.any(np.isinf(arr)):
            raise ValueError(f"{name} contains nonfinite values")
        if np.any(arr > 0):
            raise ValueError(f"{name} contains positive values")

    # Check shape consistency
    shape = logp_with_result.shape
    if logp_call_only.shape != shape or logp_no_call.shape != shape:
        raise ValueError("All input arrays must have the same shape")

    n_candidates, horizon = shape

    # Normalized decreasing future-token weights
    t = np.arange(horizon)
    raw = np.maximum(0, 1.0 - 0.2 * t)
    w_norm = raw / raw.sum()

    # Weighted negative log probabilities (loss)
    L_plus = -np.sum(logp_with_result * w_norm, axis=1)
    L_call_only = -np.sum(logp_call_only * w_norm, axis=1)
    L_no_call = -np.sum(logp_no_call * w_norm, axis=1)

    # Stronger counterfactual baseline
    L_minus = np.minimum(L_no_call, L_call_only)

    # Margin and keep mask
    margins = L_minus - L_plus
    keep = margins >= tau_filter

    return keep, margins
